summary: The Chippewa Cree Tribe, whose people call themselves Ne Hiyawak, joins two peoples. Chippewa bands once lived on both sides of today's Canadian border around the Great Lakes, and Cree territory reached from eastern Canada into Saskatchewan and Alberta. Over the 1700s and 1800s both moved west, and by the 1890s many had come together in Montana, looking for a permanent home. For years the followers of Chippewa leader Stone Child, whose name was mistranslated into English as Rocky Boy, and Cree leader Little Bear had no land of their own. They sheltered on the edges of Montana towns and on other reservations, and they suffered great hardship. With help from allies in Great Falls and Helena, the two chiefs kept pressing the federal government until 1916, when part of the old Fort Assiniboine military lands became Rocky Boy's Reservation. The reservation sits in the Bears Paw Mountains of north-central Montana. It was never allotted, and the whole of it is held in trust for the tribe. Later purchases enlarged it to about 122,000 acres. An elected Business Committee governs from Rocky Boy's Agency, and Stone Child College offers degrees close to home.
